title: Spanwit Domain Catalog v1
description: Curated, user-extensible catalog of use domains and their disk-concern entries. Catalog membership is classification metadata only: an entry's class_ceiling is a trust ceiling, never a delete authority. Executability always requires a code-registered capability with evidence and guards; catalog data cannot manufacture a deletion path.

version.description: Catalog schema version. Must be 1 for this version of the schema.

domains.description: Curated use domains. A use domain is a top-level product category of disk concerns, not a filesystem root.

entries.description: Catalog entries keyed by domain.ecosystem.name id. Each entry is classification metadata for one disk-concern location or signature-backed target.

name.description: Domain segment (first segment of entry ids).

status.description: curated: entries are wired for discovery/recipes. stub: reserved model + extension point only (no reclaim rules shipped).

id.description: Full-spine taxonomy id in domain.ecosystem.name form (e.g. development.go.go-build).

class_ceiling.description: Maximum trust an entry may carry. A prunable ceiling still requires a code-registered capability (signature) to ever produce a delete path; it is not itself deletion authority.

rebuild_expectation.description: How quickly the location refills after a manual clean.

platforms.description: Operating systems where this entry applies. Omit to apply on all platforms.

locations.description: Per-platform home-relative location hints for hotspot discovery. Go owns actual path resolution, evidence, and guards; the catalog only names where to look. Omit for signature-discovered entries (e.g. build trees under an analysis root).

signature.description: Optional link to a signature id (verified-evidence spine). Must resolve to a registered/known signature; dangling links are rejected.

recipes.description: Optional links to guided recipe ids (classification linkage only; recipes remain inert argv suggestions).

rel_home.description: Path relative to the user home directory (slash-separated; resolved per-OS by Go).
